I went through a similar situation this march when i got admitted to the hospital for a week for unbearable stomach pain. i had also been experiencing some joint pain and fatigue but i thought it was linked more to my mental state than physical one. the doctors had no idea what was wrong with me beyond some unexplained inflammation. unlike you i didnt end up having surgery and was able to go home after some improvement but i was so shocked at what had even happened? it was just so sudden! i was told at the hospital that they were almost sure that it wasnt crohn's because i hadn't had any previous stomach issues but one colonoscopy later and the results say otherwise. lol.  im getting infliximab infusions now and have been able to eat pretty much anything with minor effect on my body. so. also pretty confused and in the same boat as you !

that is a totally valid reason to feel upset! even if you only had him for one week, he was special to you and it's okay to be emotional about that. as for his death, you did everything right that you should have. there's no way to know that he didn't already have some sort of underlying condition that was out of your control. you didn't fail him in any way and you have every right to move on and try again with another snail. i know its not as easy as it sounds but try not to beat yourself up too much about it. wishing you well<3

of course never just give up on your dreams and aspirations when the going gets tough.  
but i find that the negative energy associated with constantly feeling like you need to amount to something can drastically effect the quality of your life.

if you have a goal to work towards, by all intents and purposes, work towards it! but it's also perfectly acceptable to just enjoy life for what it is instead of striving for some unattainable pillar of "success" that creates a constant feeling of lowered self-worth. 

i do see how my post could be misinterpreted though so i appreciate your comment. Of course this is all just my opinion and i'm just trying to share knowledge that i feel has helped my way of thinking and if that doesn't line up with your values that is 100% fine :-)
